description: Record an INFERENCE STEP in one call: how premises support one conclusion, and by which rule — `all` (every premise must hold, the AND a decomposition rolls up by), `any` (one is enough) or `k_of_n` with `k` (a quorum). A named rule rides `rule_name`: modus ponens is `all` over P and P → Q. `warrant` says why. reflow2 then CHECKS THAT THE CONCLUSION FOLLOWS, three-valued over each premise's computed truth (a check passing, a decision accepted, a constraint not violated; an Artifact or any other type is unknown, never guessed). A requirement, capability or interface premise reads as its OWNER'S INTENT in a step concluding a Decision (accepted holds, proposed is unknown) and by its DELIVERY in every other step; `as_intent` and `as_delivery` say it per premise. A computed result is a passing check marked `computed` whose `location` names its kept record. A blast radius names each step a changed premise reaches BROKEN or WEAKENED; get_node on the step reads its verdict; detect_gaps reports a status that claims more than its steps support. It checks the FORM, never the content. Refused, with nothing written: a bad rule or `k`, a missing premise or conclusion, and a circle. Several steps concluding a node are alternatives, read as ANY. The same id again revises the step and ADDS the premises given. For a proof: `assumed`, `discharges`, `cases`, `generalizes_over` and `independent_of`. Ask for this to say that a claim follows from other things in the design.

as_delivery.description:
Premises this step reads by their DELIVERY, by id: a requirement
delivered or met, a capability realized and checked — as every premise
read before 2026-10-24. Say it on a step concluding a Decision that
rests on delivery (a release, a go/no-go). Same rules as `as_intent`.

as_intent.description:
Premises this step reads as their OWNER'S INTENT, by id: a requirement
(accepted or met holds, proposed or deferred is unknown, dropped
fails), a capability (by the needs it SATISFIES) or an interface (by
the Decisions that govern it) — "X is required", not "X is built".
Each must be an ordinary premise of this step, named in `premises` or
already linked; a statement (a `statement_kind`, or taken as given) and
every other type read as themselves and are refused here. Unmarked, a
premise of a step concluding a Decision reads as intent already.

assumed.description:
ASSUMPTIONS this step takes up, by id — a reductio's "suppose the
primes are finite", an induction hypothesis. Each is linked as a
premise with `role: assumed`: it holds inside the argument whatever its
own truth, and everything resting on this step holds only under it
until a later step names it in `discharges`. A premise named here and
in `premises` is assumed.

cases.description:
A PROOF BY CASES: the cases' hypotheses, by id, each assumed by the
branch that proves the conclusion under it. This step discharges them
(each must be assumed beneath it, or the call is refused naming what
is). It holds only when `cases_exhaustive` names the record saying they
cover every possibility. Overwrites.

cases_exhaustive.description:
The record saying the `cases` are EXHAUSTIVE ("every integer is even or
odd"), by id — a person's word (taken as given) or a checker's (a
computed check through its kept record), never reflow2's. Drawn as a
premise of the step; refused unless it names a node. Overwrites; `""`
removes it.

claimed_by.description:
CLAIMED BY a named party: this step is that party's argument
("OpenAI's natural-language proof"), not verified here. What rests on
it reads "claimed by <party>, unverified" while nothing establishes
it; a what-if that drops it reads the claim open again. Omitted:
nothing is written.

conclusion.description:
The ONE node this step concludes. A node may be concluded by several
steps (alternative derivations, read as ANY); a step concludes one.

conclusion_form.description:
THE CONCLUSION IS MADE OF THE PREMISES AS PARTS: `conjunction` (∧I) or
`biconditional` (↔I). A what-if then reads which part still stands.

confirmed_at.description: WHEN, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Absent when unconfirmed.

confirmed_by.description:
WHO confirmed this step: a contributor id (`who:jane`) or a proof
checker's name. Absent means unconfirmed.

confirmed_how.description:
HOW: `person` (a named human), `checker` (a proof-checking program), or
omit for `unconfirmed`. A proof reads PROVEN only when every step is
confirmed.

discharges.description:
The assumptions this step DISCHARGES, by id: each must be assumed by
this step or by a step it rests on, or the call is refused naming what
is assumed beneath it. Its conclusion then no longer rests on them.
Overwrites what the step had.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

establishes.description:
WHAT RELATION THIS LINE ESTABLISHES: `entailment` (⊨, by truth table or
model) or `derivability` (⊢, by deduction). Read back; changes no truth.

generalizes_over.description:
The VARIABLES this step generalizes over, by name (`L`, `n`) — "for an
arbitrary list L". Checked: the step does not hold while anything it
rests on, at any depth, lists the variable in its `fixes`, NOR while an
undischarged assumption beneath the step names it among its variables
or fixes (or declares no variables): discharge the hypothesis first,
on this step or one beneath it. Overwrites.

id.description:
The step's id — `inf:<slug>` by convention. Calling again with an
EXISTING step's id revises it: the rule and fields you pass overwrite,
the premises you pass are ADDED (remove one with `delete_edge`), and the
conclusion must be the one it already has.

independent_except.description: The lemmas the independent lines may share, by id. Overwrites.

independent_of.description:
Other STEPS this line is stated independent of (Inference ids), e.g. a
second proof of the same claim. Checked: the lines may share no step
other than those under the lemmas in `independent_except`. Overwrites.

k.description:
For `k_of_n` only: how many premises must hold, 1 ≤ k ≤ the number of
premises. Refused on any other rule.

name.description: A short handle. Composed from the rule and the conclusion when omitted.

premises.description:
The premises, by id: any records the design holds — requirements,
checks, decisions, constraints, findings, other steps. At least one,
except for rule `immediate`, which may name none. A requirement,
capability or interface is read as its owner's INTENT in a step that
concludes a Decision, and by its DELIVERY in every other step, unless
`as_intent` or `as_delivery` says otherwise. AN ARTIFACT IS NEVER A
PREMISE (it carries no truth, so it reads unknown): a source DOCUMENTS
the claim it supports, and a COMPUTED RESULT enters as a passing
Verification marked computed whose kept calculator record (an
Artifact with its checksum) is named in the check's location, with
the result in its findings.

rule.description:
HOW THE PREMISES SUPPORT THE CONCLUSION: `all` (every premise must hold),
`any` (one is enough) or `k_of_n` (at least `k` must hold). A named rule
such as modus ponens is `all` with `rule_name`. `immediate`: NOT AN
INFERENCE — the conclusion is grasped directly (an intuition, a
self-evident or self-verifying grasp); its premises, if any, are what
it is grasped in.

rule_name.description:
The rule's own name — `modus ponens`, `induction`, `redundant sensors`.
A label: the step is checked by `rule`, never by this name.

rule_node.description:
THE NODE THAT STATES THIS STEP'S RULE, by id ("Rule RAA", an axiom of
the calculus) — a reference of its own, NEVER a premise: the step holds
only while that node holds, a what-if on it reaches every step it rules,
and it is never listed as an uncited premise. Refused when also named in
`premises`. Overwrites; `""` removes it.

warrant.description:
WHY these premises support this conclusion, in words a person can
challenge. Recorded, never judged.
